division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.23   A review officer may allow or disallow the reasonable and
proper costs of a review and fix the amount but may not make a
costs award
(a) against the client as a result of a client-requested review
unless the client’s request was unreasonable or the client
acts improperly or unreasonably at the review, or
(b) against the client as a result of a lawyer-requested review
unless the client acts improperly or unreasonably at the
review and the Court approves the costs award.

BOOK_A.title: Costs of Review
BOOK_A.commentary:
Where a lawyer got only a small fraction of the fees he claimed, he got no costs and had to
pay costs.³

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.629. It came from 1944 C. R.762(e). Cf.1914 R.761, Eng.1883 O.65 r.27, and (Imp. ) 6 & 7 Vict. c.73 s.37 para.6.

The fee award to a lawyer was under 1/20th of the amount claimed. The lawyer was denied any costs of the lawsuit over his fees. The lawyer had claimed that the client was lying and the client had made an informal offer. Party-party costs on Schedule C were increased by about 1/3: Botan v. St. Amand (#2) 2012 ABQB 260, 538 AR 306, affd 2013 ABCA 227.

BOOK_C.title: Costs of review

commentary.text: A request for review filed under rule 10.13(1) gives the review officer the authority to issue an interim or final certificate that certifies the amount of a lawyer’s charges to be paid (rule 10.19(4)(a)). It also accords the review officer the jurisdiction to make a costs award related to the review pursuant to rule 10.23.140
commentary.review_flag: (1) The commentary ('General Principles', 328 characters, no citation): 'A request for review filed under rule 10.13(1) gives the review officer the authority to issue an interim or final certificate that certifies the amount of a lawyer's charges to be paid (rule 10.19(4)(a)). It also accords the review officer the jurisdiction to make a costs award related to the review pursuant to rule 10.23.140' - the '140' after 'rule 10.23.' is a footnote number whose text is not printed (it is not a rule number), so the source of the passage is not named. It agrees with the official text: 10.13(1) (a lawyer or a client may obtain an appointment date for a review), 10.19(4)(a) (the certificate must 'certify the amount to be paid by each party or person') and 10.23 (the review officer 'may allow or disallow the reasonable and proper costs of a review'). Neither Book A nor Book B has a matching passage (Book A's note is the Botan v. St. Amand case on costs of an action). The passage is kept as printed (flagged).
